headline: A large 2021 law that sets funding and rules for roads, bridges, rail, transit, broadband, water, energy grids, and many other infrastructure areas.
what_it_does: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act provides new federal money and reauthorizes existing programs through about fiscal year 2026 for transportation, energy, water, and broadband projects. It also sets rules for things like environmental reviews, domestic-content requirements for federally funded projects, and cleanup of abandoned mines and polluted sites. The law is organized into many divisions, and it also includes tax provisions, a set of appropriations for fiscal year 2022, and a minority business development section.

who_it_affects.group: State and local governments that build or maintain roads, bridges, transit, and water systems
who_it_affects.how: They can apply for federal grants and loans for these projects, and many grants come with conditions such as American-made materials or prevailing wage requirements.
Public transit systems receive funding for buses, rail cars, and other services, which may affect service levels and vehicle upgrades in their areas.

who_it_affects.group: Households without reliable internet in rural and underserved areas
who_it_affects.how: Federal broadband grants are directed toward building service in areas that lack adequate access, and the Affordable Connectivity Benefit Program provides discounts on internet service for eligible households.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy high-speed internet plans
who_it_affects.how: Providers must display broadband consumer labels that show plan prices and whether a rate is introductory.
New vehicles must eventually include certain crash-avoidance features, and the law sets safety programs aimed at distracted and impaired driving.
The law requires a standard for automatic emergency braking on heavy trucks and creates an apprenticeship program for drivers under age 21.

who_it_affects.group: Coal communities and abandoned mine areas
who_it_affects.how: Reclamation funding is provided to clean up abandoned coal mine land, and a new program addresses abandoned hard rock mines.
The fee they pay per ton of coal into the Abandoned Mine Reclamation Fund is reduced under the law.
The law provides funding and streamlined reviews for tribal roads, bridges, and transportation safety projects.
The Minority Business Development Agency receives new authority and programs to help these businesses access capital, contracts, and grants.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that bid on federal infrastructure contracts
who_it_affects.how: They must use iron, steel, and manufactured products made in the United States on covered projects, unless a waiver applies.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed November 15, 2021; many surface transportation provisions are effective October 1, 2021, and most programs run through fiscal year 2026 or later, with some phased in on different schedules.
